title: Candeo device definition
description: A device Candeo can light, described as data: how to find it, how its reports are framed, what is sent per light, and where each light sits. Bytes are written as a capture shows them, in hexadecimal; what the frame fills in is a placeholder in braces. Guide: https://o2csi.github.io/candeo/devices-guide.html

$schema.description: This schema, for an editor's completion and checks.

name.description: The device's name, as the list of devices shows it: maker and model.

notes.description: What a reviewer should know, and where the survey says it at length. Candeo does not read them.

match.description: How the device is found among the system's HID devices. Name either the interface or the collection that carries the lighting: opening the wrong one gives a handle on which every write is lost.

interface.description: The interface of a composite device that carries the lighting: `3` on the DeathStalker.

usagePage.description: The collection's usage page, when several collections share one interface: `ff00`.

surveyed.description: The firmware version the survey was made against, `1.5`. When the inspection reads another, the device's row says so: the first lead when a device stops obeying.

inspect.description: What is asked of the device when it opens, by the name of a read written in Rust. `razer`: the firmware version, the serial, which commands the device knows, and the effect its firmware runs. Absent: nothing is asked.

report.description: The shape every report of this device shares.

wire.description: How a report leaves: `feature` (`HidD_SetFeature`) or `output` (`HidD_SetOutputReport`). A device may act on one and silently ignore the same bytes sent the other way.

length.description: The report's length in bytes, after `prefix`. Every report is padded with zeros to it; a report that could grow past it is refused when the file loads.

prefix.description: Bytes the HID API wants in front of every report and that are not part of it — usually the report id, `00` for a device without one. Offsets elsewhere in this file count from the first byte after it.

checksum.description: An integrity byte, named rather than written: `function` computed over the report's bytes `from` to `to`, both included, and written at `at`. Offsets count from the report's first byte, after `prefix`. The Razer's: `{ "function": "xor", "from": 2, "to": 87, "at": 88 }` — byte 88 is the XOR of bytes 2 to 87.

function.description: `xor`: every byte XORed together. `sum`: every byte added, modulo 256. A closed list, each function written and tested once in Candeo; a protocol needing another asks for it to be added.

command.description: Where a report carries the command it is, for a device that can say it does not know one: the inspection then refuses to send it. Offsets after `prefix`. The Razer's: class at 6, command at 7.

frame.description: The reports carrying one image of every light, sent up to thirty times a second: `open`, then `each` for the lights, then `close`.

pace.description: For a device that takes changes rather than a stream.

atLeastMs.description: The shortest gap between two images sent, in milliseconds.

skipUnchanged.description: Send nothing when the image did not change.

takeOver.description: Reports sent once when one of Candeo's effects starts on the device, to stop what its firmware animates — otherwise the firmware may keep drawing over every image.

each.description: What is sent for the lights. By default one light per report, in the grid's order; `group` and `chunk` put several in one report, `by: row` sends a row of the grid per report.

by.description: `row`: one report per row of the grid, every cell of it lit or not — a device that takes the whole grid keeps a cell left out at its last colour. Fills `{row}`, `{start}` and `{end}`.

group.description: `colour`: lights sharing a colour go together, as a device that selects lights then colours them wants. Fills `{count}` and `{addresses}`.

chunk.description: How many lights one report carries at most.

send.description: The reports sent per light, group or row. Placeholders: `{r} {g} {b}`, `{address}`, `{count}`, `{addresses}`, `{lights}`, `{row} {start} {end}`, `{length:N}`.

light.description: One light's entry, repeated where `{lights}` stands for each light of the report: `{address} {r} {g} {b}` on a device that names its keys, `{r} {g} {b}` in a row.

close.description: Reports closing an image; often what applies it.

brightness.description: The reports setting overall brightness, `{level}` from `00` (dark) to `ff`. Absent: the device offers no brightness slider.

firmware.description: The effects the device's firmware runs by itself, offered in the gallery for this device only.

send.description: The report selecting an effect: `{kind}`, and `{r} {g} {b}` and `{r2} {g2} {b2}` for its colours — the second is the first when one is given.

off.description: The kind *Off* is, when the firmware has one that shows nothing. Absent: *Off* is a black image.

id.description: The id the gallery gives it: `hardware:wave`.

colours.description: How many colours it paints with: the gallery asks for exactly as many.

send.description: Its own report, when it carries more than a kind: the Razer's wave, with its direction and speed.

name.description: What it shows, for whoever reads the file.

lights.description: Where the lights are: the positions an effect paints, the addresses the device gives them, and the rectangles the simulator draws and effects measure with.

kind.description: `keys` can be pressed, so effects reading key presses are offered; `zones` — a ring, a logo, a strip — cannot.

rows.description: The grid's rows, with `cols`: every item then gives its `row` and `col`.

cols.description: The grid's columns. Without `rows` and `cols`, the items make one row in their order.

address.description: What the device calls this light — not always its position: the Alienware keyboard counts from one.

scancode.description: What the key sends, PS/2 set 1 as Windows reports it, `e0` in front of an extended key: `1c` Enter, `e01d` right Ctrl. It is how a key press finds its light. Absent for a key that sends nothing.

shape.description: How the simulator draws it inside `rect`: the rectangle (a key, the default), a disc, or the upper or lower half of a ring.

rect.description: `[x, y, width, height]` in key units, 1 being a letter key's width, from the top left. What effects measure distances with.

name.description: What it is, for whoever reads the file.

rect.description: `[x, y, width, height]`, in the lights' units.

outline.description: Parts that light nothing — a lid, a base, ports — drawn faintly under the lights. A keyboard needs none.

colours.description: Colours per light, `rrggbb`, in the order `items` lists them; the lights past the last one given are black.

reports.description: The reports that image must give, without `prefix` and without the zeros padding them.

examples.description: Reference frames: colours in, reports out, as a capture of the device showed them. The tests replay them byte for byte — what makes a definition reviewable by someone without the device.

bytes.description: Bytes in hexadecimal, separated by spaces: `03 21 00 01 ff ff`.

report.description: A report: bytes in hexadecimal separated by spaces, and placeholders the frame fills in — `{r} {g} {b}` a colour, `{r2} {g2} {b2}` an effect's second colour, `{address}` a light's address, `{count}` how many lights the report carries, `{addresses}` their addresses, `{lights}` their entries as `each.light` writes one, `{row} {start} {end}` a row and its first and last column, `{level}` the brightness, `{kind}` a firmware effect's kind, and `{length:N}` how many bytes the report holds after offset N, worked out once it is filled.
